scope: paired initial-investigator diagnosis quality; not CFD validation or model superiority

rubric.note: Both used concrete residual, y+ and solver evidence. Sol did not reconcile the retained v5 machine-observation versus raw-log temperature discrepancy and treated retained mass-flow observations as unestablished.
Both ranked multiple plausible case-specific explanations with support, contradiction and missing evidence.

Both preserved validation, mesh, energy and readiness unknowns. Sol over-preserved one available quantity by saying measured inlet/outlet flow was not established even though the packet retained those observations; the absent item was a frozen acceptance tolerance.
Luna proposed a one-variable pressure maxIter pair. Sol proposed an unchanged fixed-length continuation before any settings comparison.
Both named observables and discriminating outcomes before execution.
Both separated solver completion, convergence, conservation, fidelity, validation and design readiness.
Both used the source methodology as a neutral method comparison rather than hidden experimental truth.
Neither changed thresholds or optimized for a green result.
Sol specified a fixed 200-iteration stop and redirect conditions. Luna called for a short pair but did not freeze an exact duration in its initial response.

outcome: Both diagnoses were strong. Luna scored one point higher on packet reconciliation; Sol defined the tighter first-test stop and selected the unchanged continuation that better addresses the still-open secular thermal evolution after the later v6-v8 record. This single case does not establish model superiority.
